newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries sit tight in London, dlr fails to stir.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries sit tight in London, dlr fails to stir.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries held steady in London on Monday as investors prepared for a batch of important data later this week, traders said.
Even the dollar's sprint overnight to its highest level since August 1994 after a weekend Group of Seven (G7) meeting failed to inspire much interest in a bond market preoccupied with raw numbers.
"It's the day before lots of big numbers start churning out and most bond markets are sitting quietly awaiting the news," Charles Quigley, bond salesman at Chase in London, said.
Releases this week include first quarter employment cost and GDP data, a report from the National Association of Purchasing Management and April payrolls.
The long bond was quoted at 93-19 at 0940 GMT, yielding 7.15 percent, compared with 93-18 in Tokyo and 93-20 at the close in New York on Friday.
June T-bond futures were quoted at 107-05, up 1/32 from Friday's settlement.

The dollar was quoted at 126.68/6.78 against the yen, off its highs but still robust after the G7's final communique talked about the risks posed by currency volatility but failed to mention the falling yen.

"The desire for G7 to get the dollar to stabilise has been kind of ignored. As ususal, foreign exchange traders seem to be inclined to test the resolve. The dollar is up but the U.S. bond market isn't really following it," Quigley said.
David Bloom, economist at HSBC James Capel in London, said Monday would likely be the calm before the storm, though he expected most of the numbers to be softer than the market's consensus.

"We are actually looking for reasonable numbers," he said, adding heavy flooding in the mid-West could take some of the punch out of the data. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
